## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle update loop combined with a fused scatter into the framebuffer can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill at N≈963 lies below the smallest measured point (N=10000), so it is not directly visible. At death_q=0.01, cost FALLS from 7.589 ns/p at N=10000 to 6.458 ns/p at N=100000 — crossing the L2 spill at N≈61680 — because per-particle startup overhead amortizes faster than the DRAM penalty bites. Past the spill, cost rises only mildly to 6.654 (N=1M) and 6.728 (N=10M): no sharp L2→DRAM knee. Raising the death rate lifts the floor uniformly — at q=0.5 the curve is nearly flat at 13.4–14.1 ns/p across all N — without reshaping the N-dependence, confirming churn adds per-particle branch cost rather than cache pressure.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 10.53 GB/s at N=100000, death_q=0.01, which is 35.2% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is compute-bound at low churn (compute=81.1% at N=100000, q=0.01) and transitions to branch-overhead-bound as death rate climbs: by q=0.5, branch_flush reaches 30.4–33.0% and compute falls to 52.5–55.0%, while bandwidth drops to 4.81–5.07 GB/s (16% of ceiling). It is never bandwidth-bound — even at the best point, backend_stall is only 12.6% and the achieved bandwidth is far below the streaming ceiling.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized LP1 component-wise within a single particle: `dup.4s v3, w10` broadcasts a coefficient, `fmul.4s v6, v17, v3` and `fadd.4s v6, v7, v6` operate on four float lanes, and `stur q6, [x9, #-0x10]` writes 128 bits back. An `ext.16b v17, v7, v16, #0xc` rearranges components, and `ld1.s {v16}[1], [x10]` is a single-element indexed load — a mild gather, not a full cross-particle gather. LP2 (the fused scatter) is entirely scalar: 12 `ldrb`/19 `strb` byte-granular framebuffer writes with 18 `csel` clamp operations and a `bl _layouts.ML01.data.Data.spawn` call per respawn. The component-wise vectorization explains the high compute fraction in LP1, but the scatter's byte stores and branchy respawn logic cap achieved bandwidth at 35% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never approaches the streaming ceiling. Peak bandwidth is 10.53 GB/s = 35% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling at N=100000, q=0.01, and the profile shows compute-bound behavior (81.1% compute) rather than bandwidth saturation. At q=0.5, branch_flush dominates at 30.4–33.0% and bandwidth collapses to 4.81 GB/s (16% of ceiling). The fused scatter's byte-granular `strb` writes and per-respawn branch logic prevent streaming regardless of death rate, so auto-vectorization of LP1 alone cannot carry the workload to the ceiling.
